citation.authors: Baird DD, Patchel SA, Saldana TM, Umbach DM et al
citation.journal: American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology

record.population: 1,693 African American women aged 23-35 with no prior fibroid diagnosis
record.design: Prospective, community-based, ultrasound at enrolment and about 18 months
record.finding: Among 1,123 fibroid-free women with follow-up, incidence was 9.4% over about 18 months, rising from 6% at ages 23-25 to 13% at 32-35. Women with existing fibroids were more than twice as likely to develop new ones (relative risk 2.3). Average fibroid growth was 89% per 18 months.
